minutes_text:
MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  MAY 21, 2024

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 6:05 p.m. at George F Canyon Nature Center, 27305 Palos
  Verdes Dr. E., Rolling Hills Estates, California, by CHAIR MCCORMICK.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR MCCORMICK led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Pope, Ciarolla, Holdsworth, Bain, Persichina,
  and McCormick

  Commissioners Absent:  Johnson

  City Staff Present:  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrow

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF APRIL 16,
  2024

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  APRIL 16, 2024.

  There being no objection, CHAIR MCCORMICK so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE.

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  FOUNDERS PARK SIGNAGE

  Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the options regarding signage to be
  placed at Founders Park (as per the agenda material).

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
May 21, 2024
   COMMISSIONER BAIN stated that she preferred sample #1 of the signage
  presented. She also stated that the photo seemed small and might need to be
  enlarged. She commented to change the word “the” to the word “its” to the verbiage
  on the sign.

  Supervisor Pinuelas noted that the photo included is a digital copy of an old photo.
  She stated that a smaller sized photo is recommended on the signage based on
  the age of the photo and possibly being unable to find a higher quality digital
  version.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that dedication of Founders Park is expected in
  September upon completion of Phase 2, in response to COMMISSIONER BAIN.

  COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH stated that he preferred sample #2 of the
  signage presented as he preferred the white contrast background with the writing.

  CHAIR MCCORMICK noted that he liked all three of the samples of the signage
  presented but liked the balance of the fencing on sample #3.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA stated that she liked sample #3 of the signage
  presented.

  Four Commissioners preferred sample #3 of the signage and two Commissioners
  preferred sample #2 of the signage. The consensus of the COMMISSION was to
  present both sample #2 and sample #3 of the signage to City Council for review.

  7.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  SUMMER 2024 SWIM PROGRAM SERVICES UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas presented an update regarding the Summer 2024 swim
  program services provided by the San Pedro & Peninsula YMCA. She provided a
  brief overview of the swimming programs offered at Peninsula High School
  between June 18 to August 10. She noted that registration started three weeks
  ago, and the classes are nearly 85% full.

  B.  MAYOR’S RIDE DEBRIEF (VERBAL REPORT)

  Coordinator Morrow presented a brief overview on the Mayor’s Ride event that
  was held on Saturday, May 11. He reported the Mayor’s Ride portion of the event
  went great with 10 dignitaries from local cities and organizations and Congressman
  Ted Lieu. There were approximately 40 members of the public joining the Mayor
  on the trail ride itself. He also stated that the Scout Pancake Breakfast held at Ernie

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
May 21, 2024
   Howlett Park from 7:00 am-11:00 am was very successful with 779 breakfasts
  served by the Scouts.

  C.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER BAIN reported that a section of fencing on the west side of Silver
  Spur Park appears to need replacement. Superintendent Goldsmith responded
  that it is on the list of fencing repairs to be completed throughout the City.

  CHAIR MCCORMICK asked if the water at the George F Canyon Reserve/Trail
  could be removed. Superintendent Goldsmith responded that maintenance is
  renting equipment which will properly redivert the water and then repair the trail.

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA asked about the equipment company used for the Beer
  and Wine Festival held at Ernie Howlett Park and shared they did a fantastic job
  with the set-up and breakdown of the event.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF APRIL 9, 2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF APRIL 23, 2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  PICKLEBALL UPDATE

  NONE.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
May 21, 2024
   B.  ASSESSMENT OF SPACE FOR POTENTIAL DOG PARK AND FUTURE PARKS

  NONE.

  11.  PARK TOURS

  A.  GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER AND RESERVE/TRAIL,
  DAPPLEGRAY PARK, FOUNDERS PARK, AND TABER GROVE

  Holly Gray, Education Director of the Palos Verdes Land Conservancy, provided
  an overview of the activities and programs offered at George F Canyon during the
  past year. She noted that attendance was at its highest level since the pandemic.
  She also stated that they started a voluntary high school internship program this
  past year that has been very well received and successful. She noted that they
  have been working with an exhibit design company to design the exhibits that will
  be displayed at the new nature center.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked about the plan for programming during construction
  of the new nature center. Ms. Gray stated that they are still developing a plan
  regarding programming and noted that some of the programming could be
  relocated to the White Point Nature Education Center and Preserve in San Pedro
  as an alternate location during the construction.

  **AT THIS POINT THE COMMISSION WALKED TO DAPPLEGRAY PARK FOR
  A TOUR**

  There were no comments made by the COMMISSION regarding Dapplegray Park
  during the park tour.

  **AT THIS POINT THE COMMISSION WALKED TO FOUNDERS PARK FOR A
  TOUR**

  Superintendent Goldsmith gave a brief overview of the landscaping construction
  currently at Founders Park. He also provided a brief overview regarding the
  installation of the play equipment for the upcoming second phase of the
  development of the park.

  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that there are plans to create six parking spaces
  along the roadside on Palos Verdes E., in response to VICE CHAIR
  PERSHICHINA.

  **AT THIS POINT THE COMMISSION DECIDED TO NOT TOUR TABER
  GROVE**

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
May 21, 2024
   12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR MCCORMICK ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 6:49 PM TO THE NEXT
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING ON JUNE 18, 2024, AT 6:00
  P.M., WHICH WILL BE HELD AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK.

  There being no objection, so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  Community Services Coordinator  Chair, Park & Activities Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
May 21, 2024
